newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Borsodchem to invest HUF 18 bln until 2000.
newsitem.headline: Borsodchem to invest HUF 18 bln until 2000.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals company Borsodchem Rt plans to invest over 18 billion forints, mostly on capacity increase, by the year 2000, company officials said on Friday.
"I hope we can finance most of that from operating cash-flow," Borsodchem general director Laszlo Kovacs told shareholders at the company's annual general meeting.
He added that Borsodchem plans to invest 4.2 billion forints this year, 6.8 billion in 1998 and seven billion in 1999.
Kovacs also said that the company plans to at least maintain sales in real terms over the next years.

The company posted 55 billion forints sales in 1996 compared with 44 billion in 1995 and the 1998 figure is planned to reach 66 billion, rising to 88 billion in 1999 and to around 97 billion in the year 2000.
Kovacs said the company is restructuring its joint venture and subsidiary portfolio in order to concentrate on the fastest-growing PVC-processing sector of window frame extrusion.
"We plan to increase the window frame output of 3,000 tonnes per year to some 10,000 tonnes in three years' time," he said.
Kovacs said that as part of the company's rationalisation plans they will reduce staff to between 2,800 and 2,900 from 3,100.
"Our goal is to reach per head per year sales of 155,000 German marks by the end of this year," Kovacs said, adding that it would be a considerable improvement over the 1991 figure of 31,000 marks.
Borsodchem shareholders approved the management's plans for a 120 forints or 12 percent dividend on the 1996 results, in addition to a 100 forints dividend advance payed in 1996.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Borsodchem shares closed at 6,530 forints, up 10.
